title: A math result you can check
thesis: OpenAI's math release passed one kind of test: a formal proof check. That test settles the exact formal statement, not whether the result is new or matters.
one_thing: So the next time an AI claim crosses your desk, ask one question: which test did it actually pass?

stories.headline: OpenAI published math manuscripts, some with proofs a computer can check
stories.happened: OpenAI released a public repository of mathematical manuscripts it says were produced by an internal model. Some results come with proofs written in Lean, a language that lets a computer check a proof.
proves: Where a formal proof exists and passes, the argument establishes its exact formal statement.
not: That the formal statement matches the paper's claim
Anything about the unformalized results, which OpenAI itself says could have issues

receipts.quote: This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model.
Some of the unformalized results could have issues.

stories.note: Repository counts are changing, so the episode leaves them out. This production did not compile the proofs.
